thread:
emma: quick brain-dump: observed several customer cases where an optimistic ack from frontdoors is visible to clients before an upstream commit finalizes, and retries from other frontdoors replay the commit. propose we add a lightweight ingress-assigned commit tag header to make commit visibility idempotent across proxies. want to capture tradeoffs and rollout plan here.

lucas: can you give the minimal sequence that trips this? a short sketch would help.

emma: sure, pasted small flow below:
```
CLIENT -> FD-A (optimistic ack) -> UPSTREAM
CLIENT -> FD-B (retry) -> FD-B forwards commit (no knowledge of FD-A ack)
UPSTREAM sees FD-B commit second -> may apply duplicate side-effect
CLIENT observed ACK from FD-A, but finalization semantics become racy
```

sofia: what's the header name? i worry about inventing headers that leak to customers.

emma: internal-only header: X-Commit-Nonce (uuid generated by ingress per commit op). semantics: ingress includes nonce; upstream persists nonce with commit (upsert semantics) and returns meta header X-Commit-Nonce-Status: accepted|seen.

lucas: nice. then FD-B sees upstream response seen -> can suppress duplicate side effects. what about streaming commits (end-of-stream trailers)?

emma: plan: 1) frontdoor still sends optimistic progress ack for latency-sensitive routes 2) when upstream returns seen|accepted, frontdoor emits final trailer commit-final:{status} so clients get deterministic final state 3) if upstream returns seen, frontdoor can emit a commit-final:duplicate trailer (instead of retracting optimistic ack) to make it non-breaking for clients that only look at first ack.

sofia: key tradeoffs: a) requires upstream changes to persist nonce atomically b) increased header surface and privacy considerations c) requires per-route opt-in for strict semantics to avoid perf regressions.

lucas: failure modes? what if upstream persistence is eventually consistent and loses the nonce? or DB rollbacks occur mid-commit?

emma: documented mitigations: persist nonce in same write transaction as the commit record. if upstream cannot do atomic persist, route should be marked eventual and FD should fall back to delayed-final semantics (delay optimistic ack until commit visible).

sofia: cache interactions: when commit nonce indicates already-seen, some frontdoors may still have older prefix in KV caches. need a cache invalidation or validation step on commit path for strict routes. proposal: per-route config commit_cache_policy: "no-op|invalidate|validate-on-read". default no-op for performance.

lucas: metrics we should collect: nonce_dup_rate, nonce_write_latency, ratio of optimistic-ack->finalize-diff, and per-route strict_failures. Also add a smoke alert when dup_rate spikes.

emma: rollout plan sketch: 1) add X-Commit-Nonce generation in frontdoor behind feature-flag 2) implement nonce handling library and helper headers for upstream teams 3) push helper lib to a few internal upstreams + staging 4) enable per-route strict|eventual config 5) monitor metrics + run a canary 6) bulk rollout after 2 weeks of stability.

sofia: operational notes: - require README for upstream teams with pseudo-code example:
```
BEGIN TRANSACTION
  if exists(commit_nonces[nonce]) return SEEN
  apply_commit_changes()
  commit_nonces[nonce] = now()
COMMIT
```
- fallback: if upstream cannot change, we keep route as eventual and optionally delay ack.

lucas: compatibility: include X-Commit-Nonce in logs/traces and add debug header X-Commit-Nonce-Status for rollout visibility. clients should ignore those headers by default.

emma: security/privacy: mark header as hop-by-hop and strip on egress to customers. only wire internally.

sofia: one more thought: for long-running streams, we should ensure the nonce is small and cheap to persist. use uuidv4 or a monotonic per-tenant counter? uuid simpler to roll out. per-tenant monotonic reduces storage but is more complex. pick uuid for initial rollout.

emma: agreed. add a follow-up RFC draft covering: header semantics, per-route config schema, cache policy, migration checklist for upstreams, metrics, and failure-mode playbook. i'll draft tomorrow.

ops-bot: Feature-flag scheduled: ingress.commit_nonce rollout to staging on 2025-07-02T09:00:00Z.
